title: Set goals with A, B, Z: a 3-5 year ambitious Z, a 3-6 month near-term B, and ignore the rest
summary: Sam Parr explains his A, B, Z goal framework: start at A, pick a near-term B 3-6 months out, and set an ambitious 3-5 year Z, working backwards from Z. Goals must be specific, include both process and outcome, and be shared for accountability. He gives finance and fitness examples and a fill-in template.

principles.text: Most successful people set goals, and getting specific about them creates breakthroughs.
principles.quote: Most successful people I’ve met set goals. And the process of getting specific about goals creates breakthroughs.

principles.text: Use A, B, Z: current start, a B about 3-6 months out, and a 3-5 year Z. Ignore the steps in between until you reach them.
principles.quote: Often, B is about 3-6 months away from your starting point (A). Z is my big, 3-5 year plan.

principles.text: A, B, Z limits distractions, since doing A and B gives you the insight to figure out later steps.
principles.quote: too often people don’t do step A or B because they’re worried about the other stops. You’ll likely figure it out when you get there because in doing A and B, you’ll gain new insight.

principles.text: Direction matters more than horsepower for ambitious people; Z is the steering wheel, and you work backwards from it.
principles.quote: For many potential winners, the issue isn’t the ability (or not) to push down on the gas pedal. Its which direction the steering wheel is pointing.

principles.text: Make goals specific and pair outcome with process, not vague aims like 'lose weight'.
principles.quote: Goals must be both process and outcome. “weigh 198 pounds by May 1st, 2026 by eating 2,000 calories a day and lifting weights 3 days a week.”

principles.text: Calibrate ambition: Z should have about a 50% chance, B about 75%, and tell a few people for accountability.
principles.quote: Goal Z should be ambitious. 50% chance of happening. Goal B should have a 75% chance of happening.
